requirements.requirement: Create the appworker account on node1.
requirements.summary: Initial discovery found no appworker account; useradd then created it with UID/GID 1000, /home/appworker owned by the account, and /bin/bash. The account and home remained present after restart.

requirements.requirement: Limit appworker login sessions to 8,192 open files and 256 processes.
requirements.summary: A root-owned limits configuration sets both soft and hard nofile limits to 8192 and nproc limits to 256. Fresh PAM-backed appworker login sessions directly reported those values before and after restart.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. The separate node-restart protocol is also complete: a healthy pre-restart account and limits state was captured, restart scheduling was acknowledged, the boot identity changed from f9031a39-89d7-426a-ae19-a60bfdcd23e1 to 9ff328c9-b90a-47e8-bc10-02260d3af929, and the running system, account, home, configuration, and effective login limits were verified after recovery. Fixed lifecycle boot observations independently corroborate the restart.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified in the chronological command trace. Creating the account was required (cmd-e3f07e4083c54278), writing and securing its limits file was required (cmd-1fc5833d9c644619), and the bounded reboot was required by the provider-wide evidence protocol (cmd-68ffcd305ac54b77). All other commands were read-only verification or expected connectivity probes during reboot. No failed services, new socket exposure, package damage, or unexplained temporary residue appeared afterward.
